A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IO-based offline reinforcement learning study. Their text, equations, tables, five result figures, technical proofs and experimental appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original quadrotor and MuJoCo evaluations in Section 4, plus fighter-jet and nonlinear temperature-control simulations in Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendix B, including benchmark comparisons, robustness tests and ablations.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects training-pair bookkeeping: v1 specifies a final training range through T-N+1 although its loop computes labels only through T-N; v2 trains on explicitly accumulated valid pairs. The residual computation, MPC experts, quadratic policy class and IO loss remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same quadrotor task, D4RL walker2d-medium and hopper-medium tasks, fighter-jet regulation and nonlinear temperature control. The disturbance-shift scenarios are also retained.

E2.justification: Evaluated comparator membership is unchanged: PPO, CQL and MPC variants for quadrotor control; CQL, IQL and COMBO for MuJoCo; and the same controller variants in Appendix B. Removing the literature classification table does not remove an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Reported experimental settings remain the same, including MuJoCo dataset sizes and 1M gradient steps, PPO's 3M environment steps, CQL's 50K iterations, MPC horizons, feature configurations and steady-state evaluation procedures. No experimental rerun or protocol revision is documented.

E4.justification: Figures 1–5 retain the same uncertainty-radius and lookback-horizon analyses, fighter-jet disturbance-shift tests, and temperature-control feature/bias ablations. Their findings and associated appendix discussions are preserved.

E5.justification: The same uncertainty-reporting practices remain: three MuJoCo training seeds and 40 evaluation seeds, four CQL seeds in Figure 1, and unchanged appendix dataset/trial counts. Reported percentile bands, medians and table uncertainty entries are retained.

E6.justification: v1 Table 2 and v2 Table 1 contain identical scores and parameter counts, including IO scores of 70.6 ± 4.2 for walker2d and 82.1 ± 11.8 for hopper in the low-data settings. Figures 1–5 retain the same curves, rankings and findings.

T1.justification: The robust-expert disturbance argument changes from w_t in v1 Equation (18) to w_{t+1} in v2 Equation (14), aligning its time index with Algorithm 1. The principal lemmas, exact SDP reformulation and Appendix A proofs otherwise retain their mathematical substance.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 reframes the learning target from approximating the true constrained-cost minimizer to distilling a non-causal nominal-model expert. The contribution statement also explicitly restricts exact robust reformulation to linear dynamics, quadratic costs and polytopic constraints. The central IO/MPC contribution remains.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly places feature engineering outside scope and describes path-dependent hindsight as providing a surrogate teacher; the exogeneity qualification already existed in v1. However, it removes v1 Remark 2.3, which explained that deployed policies lack guaranteed state-constraint satisfaction and require causal constraints.

D1.justification: v2 removes the Ok (2024) implementation citation and the paper's own repository link, while retaining the abstract's open-source-package promise. Experimental implementation details and the OfflineRL-Kit baseline link remain. This reduces the code-access information supplied by the PDF.

R1.justification: Section 1.2 substantially refocuses the research positioning. The broad control-method classification and dedicated Q-learning, regret-minimization and Willems-lemma discussions are removed. New discussion connects the work to pessimism, supervised offline RL and trajectory augmentation, including GTA, DiffStitch and model-based augmentation methods.

P1.justification: The problem statement, contribution narrative and Section 2.3 are substantially rewritten and condensed, and related work is reorganized. Algorithm 1 receives a clearer stepwise presentation. References move before the appendices, and the funding acknowledgment is removed.

P2.justification: The literature classification table is removed. The MuJoCo table is compacted and relocated, with revised subgroup headings and shorter parameter-row labels; Algorithm 1 gains line numbers. All five result figures remain, with limited caption edits and surrounding layout changes.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies the distillation target and hindsight applicability, fixes small indexing inconsistencies and updates related work. However, it removes both the explicit runtime state-constraint warning and the implementation link despite retaining the open-source promise. With the empirical evidence and main proofs unchanged, these gains in clarity coexist with losses in limitation transparency and reproducibility information, leaving no reliably assessable net quality direction.
